drivingQuestion: Is a paid bailee who broke a barrel in transit exempt by oath?
outcomeNote: baraita cited; the discussion continues past this unit

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמַּעֲבִיר חָבִית לַחֲבֵירוֹ מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם וּשְׁבָרָהּ, בֵּין שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם בֵּין שׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר – יִשָּׁבַע, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם – יִשָּׁבַע, נוֹשֵׂא שָׂכָר – יְשַׁלֵּם. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: זֶה וְזֶה יִשָּׁבַע, וְתָמֵיהַּ אֲנִי אִם יְכוֹלִין זֶה וָזֶה לִישָּׁבַע.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «The Sages taught:» With regard to «one who was transporting a barrel for another» person «from one place to another and he broke it, whether» he was «an unpaid bailee or a paid bailee,» if «he takes an oath» that he was not negligent, he is exempt from payment. This is «the statement of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehuda says: An unpaid bailee takes an oath» and does not pay, but «a paid bailee pays. Rabbi Eliezer says: This» one «and that» one «take an oath, and I wonder whether» both «this one and that one can take an oath.»
